steps.title: Identify the noun’s case role
steps.body: In the supplied Муж говорит, the husband is the subject and the talking verb states its action. The subject noun is nominative. Recognizing the English sentence meaning is useful, but the role check asks whether the noun is a subject or direct object. Do not guess nominative merely because a case is unfamiliar.

steps.title: Separate the subject from its description
steps.body: In Поезд старый, the train is the subject noun and old is its predicate description. This present property clause has no overt Russian copula. The noun’s case role is nominative subject, not accusative direct object. A dictionary-looking noun or familiar translation alone does not identify its role in every construction.

steps.title: Apply the distinction to a different supplied noun

steps.title: Nouns that keep their form
steps.body: An indeclinable noun keeps the same form for case or number. In these examples, ра́дио and такси́ are indeclinable. Recognize the behavior of the shown noun.

steps.title: Four more unchanged nouns
steps.body: The nouns метро́, кино́, пальто́ and ко́фе are also indeclinable. Their forms stay unchanged for case or number. Learn the noun with this behavior; do not infer that every noun with a similar ending behaves the same way.

steps.title: Recognize the behavior

steps.title: The possessor and the possessed thing
steps.body: In the simple possession pattern shown here, the possessor after the possession preposition is genitive. The thing possessed is nominative. The schematic slot in the first example represents that possessed thing. У меня есть Х — I have X. У вас есть сын? — Do you have a son?

steps.title: Possession versus absence
steps.body: A simple positive possession line places the possessed thing in the nominative. An absence line places the absent thing in the genitive. Decide whether the whole shown line affirms or denies possession.

steps.title: Positive statements and questions
steps.body: The son examples keep the same simple possession pattern in a statement or question: genitive possessor and nominative possessed thing. The form of a question does not turn the noun into an absence construction. Да, у меня есть сын. — Yes, I have a son. У твоего́ му́жа есть оди́н друг — Your husband has one friend.

steps.title: Keep quantity and absence separate
steps.body: The many-friends example includes a quantity expression. Quantity patterns are separate from the simple nominative possessed thing in the son checks. У меня́ нет сы́на — No, I don't have a son.

steps.title: Identify absence
steps.body: In an absence line, the absent thing is genitive. An absence line may describe what a person does not have or what does not exist at a place. У меня́ нет сы́на — No, I don't have a son. Нет рестора́нов — There are no restaurants.

steps.title: Choose a complete case explanation
steps.body: The absence construction uses a genitive noun for the absent thing. The simple positive possession construction instead uses a genitive possessor and a nominative possessed thing. Choose from the meaning and construction of the whole supplied line.

steps.title: Apply the absence pattern
steps.body: Both negative examples below use the genitive for the absent thing. Keep the absent thing separate from any possessor or place mentioned in the line. В Москве́ нет ста́рых зда́ний — There are no old buildings in Moscow. У моего́ бра́та нет де́нег — My brother doesn't have any money.

steps.title: Aspect and time
steps.body: Aspect describes how an action is viewed, not when it happens. Imperfective can focus on an activity, repetition, or the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint. Perfective presents an event with its boundary or result. Imperfective does not by itself mean unfinished. говори́ть is imperfective; сказа́ть is perfective. These infinitives do not specify tense on their own.

steps.title: The saying and telling pair
steps.body: Many Russian verbs are learned in an aspect pair, but not every verb has two words, and a pair is not automatic. говорить and сказать are context-dependent counterparts, not a universal pair for the English verb speak. For the saying/telling pair shown here, the perfective counterpart of говори́ть is сказа́ть; the imperfective counterpart of сказа́ть is говори́ть. These checks ask you to recognize this vocabulary pair, not choose aspect in a sentence.

steps.title: A worked doing and making pair
steps.body: де́лать is imperfective; сде́лать is perfective. Both concern doing or making. The perfective focuses on accomplishing the action; the imperfective can describe the activity or its occurrence without that focus. Given де́лать and a request for its perfective counterpart, choose сде́лать. говори́ть concerns speaking or saying and belongs to the other pair. Learn the shown pair rather than assuming every prefix changes only aspect.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the counterpart from the saying/telling pair. Then compare its aspect and meaning with the other option.

steps.body: хоро́ший — good. хоро́шее — good.

steps.title: Admitted instruction
steps.body: This states that, if the stem ends in '''ж, ц, ч, ш''', or '''щ''', any unstressed '''o''' in an ending is instead written as '''e'''. For example, 'the good letter' is written '''хорошее письмо''' (and ''not'' '''хорошое письмо''').

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the admitted record. The feedback states the frozen field.

steps.title: Remediation
steps.body: This states that, if the stem ends in '''ж, ц, ч, ш''', or '''щ''', any unstressed '''o''' in an ending is instead written as '''e'''. For example, 'the good letter' is written '''хорошее письмо''' (and ''not'' '''хорошое письмо''').

items.prompt: Which admitted row is the neuter form?
items.feedback: хоро́шее is the nominative singular neuter form of this adjective. хоро́шая is feminine singular. The adjective agrees with the gender of the noun it modifies; the neuter form requested here is also the form used with the neuter noun in the good-letter example.
distractorRationales: хоро́шая is feminine singular, not the requested neuter form.

distractorDifference: хоро́шая is feminine singular, not the requested neuter form.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: хоро́шее is the nominative singular neuter form of this adjective. хоро́шая is feminine singular. The adjective agrees with the gender of the noun it modifies; the neuter form requested here is also the form used with the neuter noun in the good-letter example.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the rejected spelling rather than the accepted example?
items.feedback: хорошое письмо is the rejected spelling requested by this question. Its unstressed adjective ending uses o where the five-letter rule requires e after the stem-final consonant transliterated sh. хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling. The keyed counterexample is incorrect Russian, not a form to use.
distractorRationales: хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling, while this question asks you to identify the rejected spelling.

distractorDifference: хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling, while this question asks you to identify the rejected spelling.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: хорошое письмо is the rejected spelling requested by this question. Its unstressed adjective ending uses o where the five-letter rule requires e after the stem-final consonant transliterated sh. хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling. The keyed counterexample is incorrect Russian, not a form to use.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the accepted spelling rather than the rejected example?
items.feedback: хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling in the source example. The adjective stem ends in the consonant transliterated sh; its unstressed neuter ending uses e rather than o under the five-letter spelling rule. хорошое письмо is the rejected counterexample and should not be used as correct Russian.
distractorRationales: хорошое письмо is the rejected spelling: it uses o where this unstressed adjective ending requires e.

distractorDifference: хорошое письмо is the rejected spelling: it uses o where this unstressed adjective ending requires e.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling in the source example. The adjective stem ends in the consonant transliterated sh; its unstressed neuter ending uses e rather than o under the five-letter spelling rule. хорошое письмо is the rejected counterexample and should not be used as correct Russian.
